articles.title: Maersk expands Gemini network overhaul
articles.summary: Maersk has announced a broad series of changes across the Gemini network, including the launch of the AE18 service and revised rotations for AE2, AE11, AE12, AE19 and ME2. The changes follow the structural rerouting of Gemini’s Asia–Mediterranean services through the Suez Canal. They will reshape the network’s...
articles.body: Maersk has announced a broad series of changes across the Gemini network, including the launch of the AE18 service and revised rotations for AE2, AE11, AE12, AE19 and ME2. The changes follow the structural rerouting of Gemini’s Asia–Mediterranean services through the Suez Canal. They will reshape the network’s coverage of North Europe, the Mediterranean, the Middle East, Sri Lanka and the Adriatic. The new AE18 will operate alongside AE19 to consolidate West Mediterranean hub coverage. The wider configuration will also support connections from Asia to West Africa and the East Coast of Latin America. Maersk introduces AE18 service The AE18 will consolidate the Tangier and Algeciras coverage previously provided through AE2, AE12 and AE11 while introducing a direct call at Xiamen. The new rotation will be: Shanghai – Xiamen – Tanjung Pelepas – Algeciras – Tangier – Algeciras – Xiamen Maersk Edirne, operating voyage 647W, will inaugurate the service from Shanghai on 22 November 2026. AE2, AE11 and AE19 rotations revised The AE2 service will replace its westbound Tangier call with Rotterdam, providing an additional connection from Ningbo and Shanghai to the Dutch port. The revised arrangement will begin with Moscow Maersk voyage 646W, departing Ningbo on 15 November 2026. AE11 will add a westbound call at Salalah and replace its westbound Tangier call with Port Said. Estelle Maersk voyage 647W will be the first affected sailing, departing Shanghai on 17 November. AE19 will replace Shanghai with Nansha and add Damietta to its rotation. The changes will begin with Ane Maersk voyage 647W, departing Xingang on 18 November. The revised ME2 rotation will be: Ennore – Colombo – Suez Canal – Algeciras – Rotterdam – London Gateway – Hamburg – Tangier – Suez Canal – Jeddah – Colombo Maersk Tukang voyage 649E will be the first affected sailing. The vessel is scheduled to arrive in Jeddah on 20 December 2026. The new call will provide direct connectivity to Saudi Arabia from Rotterdam, London Gateway and Hamburg. Colombo transfers from AE15 to AE12 Maersk will also transfer the Colombo call from AE15 to AE12, creating a connection between the Adriatic ports of Koper and Rijeka and Sri Lanka. Cargo moving through Colombo will gain access to onward connections covering South India and Bangladesh. articles.title: EMGS lands offshore exploration survey award in Pakistan
articles.summary: Norwegian geophysical services specialist Electromagnetic Geoservices (EMGS) has secured a letter of award from Pakistan’s Mari Energies for controlled-source electromagnetic surveys across multiple offshore exploration blocks. articles.body: Asia Europe Offshore EMGS lands offshore exploration survey award in Pakistan Bojan Lepic October 19, 2026 0 0 1 minute read Norwegian geophysical services specialist Electromagnetic Geoservices (EMGS) has secured a letter of award from Pakistan’s Mari Energies for controlled-source electromagnetic surveys across multiple offshore exploration blocks. The Oslo-based company said the programme would combine CSEM-derived resistivity information with seismic and geological data to improve prospect evaluation, reduce exploration uncertainty and support decisions on future drilling targets. The survey is expected to take place in the first quarter of 2027. The agreement follows meetings between senior EMGS representatives, Mari Energies’ management and technical teams, and the Pakistani company’s offshore joint-venture partners, including Turkish Petroleum. Mari Energies said it intends to use electromagnetic technology to evaluate, rank and de-risk exploration prospects as it seeks to unlock Pakistan’s largely unexplored offshore hydrocarbon potential. In May, the country finalised agreements covering 23 offshore exploration blocks spanning approximately 54,600 sq km in the Indus and Makran basins, with initial investment commitments of $82m. Mari Energies emerged as the largest participant in the licensing round, securing operatorship of 18 blocks and non-operating interests in another five. articles.summary: Petronas and Petrovietnam are expanding their 35-year partnership across LNG, upstream development, and low-carbon energy arsenal in Vietnam.
articles.body: Collaboration October 19, 2026 · 24 minutes ago Petronas and Petrovietnam strengthen ties in pursuit of energy security and low-carbon growth Petronas and Petrovietnam are expanding their 35-year partnership across LNG, upstream development, and low-carbon energy arsenal in Vietnam. MC Melisa Cavcic Senior Editor 2 minutes read LinkedIn X Email The signing of a strategic alliance agreement (SAA) between Petronas and Petrovietnam Source: Petronas Asian energy giants Malaysia's Petronas and Vietnam National Industry – Energy Group (Petrovietnam) have forged a strategic alliance agreement (SAA) to supercharge Vietnam's energy security, expand liquefied natural gas (LNG) infrastructure, and accelerate low-carbon solutions across the region. The SAA was signed at Petrovietnam’s headquarters by Tan Sri Tengku Muhammad Taufik , Petronas’ President and Group Chief Executive Officer, and Le Manh Cuong , Petrovietnam’s President and Chief Executive Officer, reaffirming the commitment of both companies to deepen industry cooperation in support of Vietnam’s energy security and long-term development. This agreement establishes a forward-looking framework for both organizations to leverage their respective strengths and pursue opportunities across the energy value chain, spanning upstream development, gas and LNG, and downstream opportunities, as well as low-carbon solutions. The duo’s signing of a strategic alliance agreement is said to mark a new milestone in 35 years of collaboration and reaffirms their shared commitment to advancing energy security, sustainability, and long-term value creation. This longstanding partnership has also extended towards regional energy collaboration, including the tripartite renewable energy initiative between Vietnam, Malaysia, and Singapore, where Malaysia serves both as a power transit hub and a demand center, alongside Singapore as a key demand center. “Petronas remains committed to working with Petrovietnam to support Vietnam’s evolving energy needs while unlocking opportunities for broader energy cooperation across the region,” underlined the Malaysian giant. articles.title: Ithaca Energy chief executive to retire
articles.summary: UK North Sea oil and gas producer Ithaca Energy has launched a search for a new chief executive after Luciano Vasques announced plans to retire by March 31, 2027. The company said its board has begun identifying a successor, with a further announcement to follow in due course to allow an orderly transition of...
articles.body: Europe Offshore Ithaca Energy chief executive to retire Bojan Lepic October 19, 2026 0 24 1 minute read Ithaca Energy Ithaca Energy UK North Sea oil and gas producer Ithaca Energy has launched a search for a new chief executive after Luciano Vasques announced plans to retire by March 31, 2027. The company said its board has begun identifying a successor, with a further announcement to follow in due course to allow an orderly transition of responsibilities. Vasques has led Ithaca Energy since October 2024, when he took the helm following the company’s transformational combination with Eni’s UK upstream oil and gas business. His departure comes after a period of significant expansion for the London-listed producer, including its entry into the FTSE 100 index in September this year. “I believe the Company is in excellent shape and that now is the right time for me to retire and hand over the reins,” Vasques said. The leadership change also comes shortly after Ithaca announced a $860m deal to acquire offshore oil assets in eastern Canada from Suncor Energy, with up to $250m in additional payments linked to oil prices. The transaction, expected to close in the first half of 2027, marks the company’s first international acquisition. Vasques joined Ithaca after serving as managing director of Eni UK, where he oversaw the acquisition and integration of Neptune Energy’s UK business. Before that, he headed Eni’s Central Asia operations, overseeing the Italian energy major’s interests in Kazakhstan’s giant Kashagan and Karachaganak oil and gas fields. The industry veteran has more than 30 years of experience in technical, operational and executive roles. He also serves on the board of Offshore Energies UK, the country’s offshore industry body. articles.title: 'World’s first' commercial ship-to-ship green ammonia bunkering performed in China
articles.summary: The world's first commercial ship-to-ship bunkering of green ammonia fuel, as China Energy Engineering Group (Energy China) describes it, has...
articles.body: Vessels October 19, 2026 · 53 minutes ago 'World’s first' commercial ship-to-ship green ammonia bunkering performed in China NS Nadja Skopljak Managing Editor 2 minutes read LinkedIn X Email CMB.TECH The world's first commercial ship-to-ship bunkering of green ammonia fuel, as China Energy Engineering Group (Energy China) describes it, has been completed in China. The operation was performed on October 13 at an anchorage in Zhoushan Port, Zhejiang Province, jointly by Energy China Hydrogen Energy, Belgium’s CMB.TECH and Jiangsu Andefu Energy Technology. From Energy China's HyFlow-1 Songyuan Hydrogen Energy Industrial Park project, a total of 1,000 tons of green ammonia was loaded through the dedicated liquid ammonia bunkering vessel Shenghang Yongle onto CMB.TECH's ammonia-powered ship, Mineral Europa . To make the ship-to-ship bunkering operation possible, Jiangsu Andefu Energy Technology obtained a liquid ammonia bunkering license from the Zhoushan municipal government in May, after which Shenghang Yongle completed its conversion for bunkering functions in August and was assigned the class notation “Ammonia Bunkering” by China Classification Society (CCS). Following bunkering, Mineral Europa will leave Zhoushan and cross the Pacific to Australia for commercial service. According to Energy China, the operation achieved several world firsts, including the first commercial ship-to-ship green ammonia bunkering at anchorage, the first dedicated ammonia bunkering vessel placed in service, and the first license for ship-to-ship liquid ammonia bunkering put into use. All the used green ammonia came from Energy China’s integrated green hydrogen, ammonia and methanol project in Songyuan, Jilin Province. Phase I of the project, which entered formal operation in December 2025, converts wind and solar power into green marine fuel through renewable power generation, water electrolysis for hydrogen, and green ammonia synthesis. The project has secured a sales contract for green ammonia for ocean-going shipping. So far, 7,000 tons of green ammonia produced by the Songyuan project have reached the Nanjing Port tank farm and will be bunkered in batches as planned. Reach the Offshore Energy industry in one go! articles.title: COSCO Shipping Ports throughput jumps in September
articles.summary: COSCO Shipping Ports handled 11.04 million TEUs across its global terminal portfolio in September 2026, representing a 15.7% increase compared with the same month last year. The latest performance lifted the terminal operator’s total container throughput for the first nine months of the year to 93.91 million TEUs, up...
articles.body: COSCO Shipping Ports handled 11.04 million TEUs across its global terminal portfolio in September 2026, representing a 15.7% increase compared with the same month last year. The latest performance lifted the terminal operator’s total container throughput for the first nine months of the year to 93.91 million TEUs, up 8.5% year on year. Third-quarter throughput reached 32.60 million TEUs, marking an annual increase of 9.2%. Overseas terminals drive COSCO Shipping Ports growth Overseas terminals excluding Container Terminal Tollerort handled 3.56 million TEUs in September, an increase of 20.7% from the corresponding month of 2025. Their cumulative throughput reached 31.48 million TEUs during the January–September period, rising 18.9% year on year. Piraeus Container Terminal handled 366,600 TEUs in September, up 15.3% year on year. Its nine-month throughput increased by 1.7% to approximately 3.09 million TEUs. Suez Canal Container Terminal processed 540,300 TEUs during the month, representing growth of 4%. Its cumulative volume reached 4.70 million TEUs, up 17.3%. Meanwhile, CSP Chancay Terminal handled 46,700 TEUs in September, an increase of 25% compared with the same month last year. Throughput during the first nine months reached 341,400 TEUs, rising 47.3%. Chinese terminal portfolio records mixed performance Within China, the Pearl River Delta portfolio handled 2.77 million TEUs in September, up 22.6% year on year. Nine-month throughput increased by 6.9% to 23.88 million TEUs. The Southwest Coast recorded September throughput of 1.05 million TEUs, representing annual growth of 24.9%. Its cumulative volume remained broadly stable at 7.24 million TEUs. Southeast Coast terminals reported a 23.6% monthly increase to 556,100 TEUs, while the Yangtze River Delta portfolio handled 1.55 million TEUs, up 6.8%. Bohai Rim throughput declined by 2.4% in September to 1.55 million TEUs, although its nine-month volume remained 3.9% higher at 14.06 million TEUs.

articles.title: Norway ends one offshore wage row only for Reach Subsea strike to begin
articles.summary: Norway’s protracted offshore well services wage dispute has been settled through voluntary arbitration, even as a separate labour conflict has triggered a strike at subsea contractor Reach Subsea. An arbitration panel has ruled that wage and other provisions previously agreed under the Oil Services Agreement between...
articles.body: Europe Offshore Norway ends one offshore wage row only for Reach Subsea strike to begin Bojan Lepic October 19, 2026 0 70 1 minute read Reach Subsea Reach Subsea Norway’s protracted offshore well services wage dispute has been settled through voluntary arbitration, even as a separate labour conflict has triggered a strike at subsea contractor Reach Subsea. An arbitration panel has ruled that wage and other provisions previously agreed under the Oil Services Agreement between employers’ organisation Offshore Norge and trade union Styrke will also apply to the Well Services Agreement between Offshore Norge and SAFE. The decision ends a dispute that sparked a month-long strike and lockout over the summer before the parties agreed on July 14 to refer the matter to arbitration. The ruling covers changes to wage rates and union funds, with the new terms taking effect retrospectively from July 14 and remaining in force until May 31, 2028. SAFE expressed disappointment that the panel rejected its demand to maintain a separate agreement for members employed by SLB. However, the union welcomed the decision to backdate wage adjustments and other payments rather than apply them only from the date of the ruling. Despite the settlement, industrial unrest continues elsewhere in Norway’s offshore services sector. Reach Subsea confirmed that mediation with SAFE ended at midnight on October 16 without an agreement, prompting six offshore employees covered by the SAFE Offshore Collective Agreement to walk out on strike. The Haugesund-based company said it was assessing the operational and financial implications of the industrial action while staying focused on maintaining safe, efficient operations across its projects. Reach added that it remained committed to constructive dialogue with SAFE and finding a mutually acceptable solution as soon as possible. Norway’s national mediator confirmed that the parties remained too far apart for a settlement proposal likely to be accepted by both sides. The developments follow another wage settlement reached on Friday, when SAFE and Delta struck a deal with Offshore Norge and Norsk Industri over the separate Oil Agreement. That agreement, reached after mediation ran approximately two hours beyond the deadline, averted a threatened strike and lockout. articles.title: Northern Sea Route Transits Surpass 2025 Total as Arctic Shipping Gains Momentum
articles.summary: The number of commercial transit voyages through Russia’s Northern Sea Route (NSR) had already surpassed the full-year 2025 total by the end of September, putting Arctic shipping on course for another record season as cargo volumes rise and more vessels test the route between Asia and Europe.

(Source: Atomflot) Cargo volumes rise as tanker, bulk carrier and container traffic expand, with 2026 transits potentially reaching 150. The number of commercial transit voyages through Russia’s Northern Sea Route (NSR) surpassed the full-year 2025 total by the end of September, putting Arctic shipping on course for another record season. The Centre for High North Logistics (CHNL) identified 104 confirmed transit voyages through Sept. 30, compared with 103 during the entire 2025 navigation season and 97 in 2024 . Estimated transit cargo reached 3.7 million metric tons, up 15% from 3.2 million tons for all of 2025. The combined deadweight tonnage of vessels completing transits reached approximately 7.8 million tons, 26% higher than the 6.2 million tons recorded in 2025, according to CHNL’s analysis of AIS data from MarineTraffic by Kpler. The center estimates that the final 2026 total could approach 150 transits and exceed 4.5 million tons of cargo. Those figures remain provisional: as of Sept. 30, another 45 potential voyages were either underway or within the NSR area and could still qualify as completed transits. Tankers remained the largest cargo segment, with 22 eastbound voyages carrying an estimated 2.1 million tons, primarily crude oil. Murmansk was the main departure point, followed by Primorsk and Ust-Luga, highlighting the route’s role in moving Russian oil from Baltic ports toward Asian markets. Bulk carriers also recorded substantial activity. Thirteen eastbound voyages carried an estimated 1.1 million tons of cargo, while 27 westbound voyages reflected a significant repositioning of vessels toward the Baltic, Murmansk and other western destinations. The pattern underscores how the NSR serves not only as a cargo corridor but also as a seasonal route for moving commercial tonnage between operating regions. Container shipping offered another indication of the route’s evolving use. CHNL recorded 13 container ship transits by the end of September, including voyages between Asian and European ports that did not originate or terminate in Russia. Four international Asia-Europe transits had been completed, compared with just one during the entire 2025 season. Among them, the container ships Panstar Acro and Dubai Tower reached the United Kingdom from South Korea and China, respectively, while Riyadh Mukaab sailed from China to Felixstowe. The bulk carrier Nan Xin 27 completed a voyage from China to Klaipeda, Lithuania. Although still a small share of total NSR traffic, these voyages demonstrate growing interest in using the Arctic as an alternative Asia-Europe corridor. Ice conditions shaped the season’s development. During the first half of August, significant traffic diverted north of the Severnaya Zemlya archipelago , bypassing the conventional route through the Vilkitsky Strait. Conditions improved later in August, allowing traffic to return toward the traditional passage as open water expanded along the route. By early September, a more continuous open-water corridor had developed across much of the NSR. The late-season conditions were more favorable for continued navigation than in 2024 and 2025, when ice formation ended the navigation period early . Open-water conditions persisted beyond Sept. 30 this year, although seasonal freeze-up was expected to progressively restrict vessels without ice-class capabilities from mid-October onward. articles.summary: Ocean Oilfield has wrapped up the acquisition of a rig, which is now docked in Malta and ready for immediate global deployment.
articles.body: Business & Finance October 19, 2026 · 1 hour ago Jack-up changes hands as Ocean Oilfield enriches its drilling fleet with Noble’s rig Ocean Oilfield has wrapped up the acquisition of a rig, which is now docked in Malta and ready for immediate global deployment. MC Melisa Cavcic Senior Editor 2 minutes read LinkedIn X Email Ocean MVM jack-up rig Source: Ocean Oilfield Abu Dhabi-headquartered Ocean Oilfield Integrated Solutions has upgraded its fleet lineup by finalizing the takeover of a jack-up rig from Noble Corporation, a U.S.-based offshore drilling giant. This move boosts the UAE player's capacity to take on offshore projects worldwide. Noble revealed a six-rig divestment last year , which entailed the sale of the Noble Resolve rig to Ocean Oilfield Drilling for $64 million in cash. The closing of the transaction was expected in Q2 2026, upon conclusion of the jack-up’s existing contract. Ocean Oilfield has confirmed the completion of the acquisition and ownership takeover of Ocean MVM , formerly Noble Resolve, which is a GustoMSC CJ50-X100 MC jack-up drilling rig. Ocean MVM arrived in Malta on October 13, 2026, and is now being actively marketed and made available for immediate deployment, subject to contractual arrangements and operational requirements. The new owner emphasizes that this rig presents an attractive opportunity for operators seeking a capable, high-efficiency jack-up drilling unit for upcoming offshore campaigns worldwide. The UAE-based company emphasized: “The GustoMSC CJ50-X100 MC design series is recognised for its high structural efficiency, optimised safety footprint and reliable performance in challenging offshore and severe weather conditions. “This strategic acquisition marks another significant milestone in Ocean Oilfield’s continued growth and expansion of its offshore drilling capabilities.” Ocean MVM jack-up rig Source: Ocean Oilfield via LinkedIn Ocean MVM jack-up rig Source: Ocean Oilfield via LinkedIn Ocean MVM jack-up rig Source: Ocean Oilfield via LinkedIn With Ocean MVM officially joining the Ocean Oilfield fleet, the acquisition is said to further strengthen the drilling player’s asset portfolio and reinforce its commitment to delivering reliable, cost-effective offshore drilling solutions tailored to its clients’ operational requirements. articles.summary: A carrier loaded with Qatari liquefied natural gas is sailing north through the Red Sea, potentially speeding up delivery to European customers with a rare transit through waters vulnerable to renewed attacks from Houthi rebels.

Photo: RasGas By Stephen Stapczynski Oct 19, 2026, (Bloomberg) –A carrier loaded with Qatari liquefied natural gas is sailing north through the Red Sea, potentially speeding up delivery to European customers with a rare transit through waters vulnerable to renewed attacks from Houthi rebels. The tanker, which loaded an LNG cargo in Qatar in August, is signaling Poland as its next destination, according to ship-tracking data compiled by Bloomberg. Poland’s Orlen SA has a long-term supply contract with QatarEnergy, though shipments under the deal were canceled after the exporter’s giant Ras Laffan plant was hit by drone strikes in March. The transit — which comes as European natural gas prices hit the highest level in almost four years — is unusual. Commercial vessels have increasingly tended to take long detours to avoid the Red Sea, typically sailing around Africa’s Cape of Good Hope to head to Europe, a route that can add almost two weeks and extra costs to a one-way journey. UK Maritime Trade Operations, a security outfit which links commercial shipping and military forces, reported on Saturday that an unnamed LNG tanker was approached southeast of the Yemeni port of Al Mukalla, in the Gulf of Aden, by a skiff that fired two shots. The tanker’s security team fired two shots in return. UKMTO did not provide further details, though ship-tracking data suggest the Poland-bound carrier was the only LNG tanker in the region at the time. The data suggests the vessel has since continued its journey. QatarEnergy did not immediately respond to requests for comment. For shipments from China, CMA CGM said the charges are subject to filing requirements and may be included in the ocean freight rate. The measure excludes northeastern Brazil. The surcharge will be US$700 per 20-foot container and US$900 per 40-foot container. It covers shipments to Northern Europe, the Mediterranean, Adriatic, Black Sea, North Africa, Middle East and Red Sea. Northern Europe includes the Baltic and Scandinavian markets. Shipments from Rosario, Argentina, to the Middle East Gulf are excluded. CMA CGM will also introduce a surcharge of €250 per TEU for refrigerated containers moving from Morocco to West Africa. This charge will take effect on November 1 and remain in place until further notice. articles.title: Twelve Migrants Die in Two Boat Capsizings Off Greek Islands
articles.summary: Twelve migrants drowned in two separate incidents off the Greek islands of Lesbos and Samos in the northeastern Aegean Sea on Monday, after their boats capsized as the coast guard chased them, authorities said.Five men and one woman died after…
articles.body: Twelve Migrants Die in Two Boat Capsizings Off Greek Islands Maritime Activity Reports, Inc. October 19, 2026 © Aleksandr S / Adobe Stock Twelve migrants drowned in two separate incidents off the Greek islands of Lesbos and Samos in the northeastern Aegean Sea on Monday, after their boats capsized as the coast guard chased them, authorities said. Five men and one woman died after a speedboat carrying migrants from Turkey made a sudden manoeuvre and overturned roughly four nautical miles north of Samos, the Greek coast guard said. Fourteen men survived and a search-and-rescue operation was under way. Authorities arrested one of the survivors, an Iranian national, on suspicion of migrant smuggling. Earlier, four men, one woman and an infant died when their boat collided with a Greek coast guard vessel and overturned off the area of Agrilia in Lesbos. Eight survivors were taken to hospital. Authorities arrested a 37-year-old Turkish national who was among the eight survivors and identified him as the suspected smuggler and operator of the boat. The government vowed "zero tolerance" towards migrant smugglers, whom it blamed for the deaths. On the incident off Lesbos, Greece's shipping minister Vassilis Kikilias said evidence so far indicated the speedboat struck the left side of a coast guard vessel with its bow, adding that the exact circumstances were under investigation. "Our position is non-negotiable: zero tolerance for smugglers," he said in a post on X. Greece, for years a favored gateway to Europe for migrants and refugees from the Middle East, Africa and Asia, was at the front line of Europe's migration crisis in 2015-2016 and nearly 1 million people landed on its islands, mainly from Turkey. It has since toughened its stance and has been accused by human rights groups of forcibly returning migrants and asylum-seekers on its sea and land borders, a practice it denies, saying its coast guard acts with full respect for human lives and rights. Splash first reported the Swiss group’s interest in Mangalia in June 2025, with cruise ships, ropax vessels and tugboats among the potential construction opportunities. Rheinmetall subsequently confirmed in May this year that the two companies were exploring a joint takeover. The latest deal comes as MSC is also pursuing a potential investment in Germany’s Meyer Werft, the cruise shipbuilder in which federal and regional governments hold an 80% stake. Mangalia, which boasts three drydocks, entered insolvency in June 2024 following a protracted dispute between Dutch shipbuilder Damen and the Romanian government over management rights. The acquisition offers the yard a route back to large-scale construction while potentially giving MSC a significant new foothold in European shipbuilding. In its latest weekly report, broker Hartland estimates that independent owners of VLCCs, suezmaxes and aframaxes/LR2s are collectively generating around $400m in daily profits above what they budgeted at the start of 2026. For context, the world’s containerlines made an estimated $150bn in 2022, their most profitable year on record. Five-year-old VLCCs are now valued at $218m, a record 55% premium over a newbuilding Meanwhile, VLCC earnings on the Middle East Gulf-China route have breached $1.3m a day, according to Veson Nautical. The astonishing freight market is producing equally remarkable asset valuations. Veson reports that a 15-year-old VLCC was valued above a newbuilding for the first time at the end of September, while its latest data shows values for vessels of this age surging 196% year-on-year to $163.2m. Five-year-old VLCCs are now valued at $218m, a record 55% premium over a newbuilding. Poten & Partners puts the premium for prompt resale tonnage even higher, assessing an immediately available VLCC at $235m against $130m for a newbuilding delivering in 2029. Middle Eastern buyers are increasingly paying whatever it takes to secure tonnage. Veson recorded 34 tanker purchases by regional interests between July 1 and October 5, up from 21 a year earlier, including 19 VLCCs compared with just one previously. Poten observed that at current earnings, the extraordinary premiums paid for secondhand ships can be recovered remarkably quickly. “The market shows eye-popping numbers for secondhand tonnage, but based on current rates, it does not take long to earn back the premium that you have to pay (if somebody is willing to sell you a ship),” Poten stated in its latest weekly report. And while much has been written about the giant tanker orderbook casting a shadow over the markets, that is not an immediate threat, especially for VLCCs. Hartland noted that despite 319 VLCCs being on order, just 20 are scheduled for delivery over the six months covering the fourth quarter and first quarter of 2027. articles.title: Hormuz attacks overwhelm UKMTO
articles.summary: The sheer volume of attacks on commercial shipping around the Strait of Hormuz has left Britain’s maritime security reporting centre struggling to keep track, with most vessels targeted in the increasingly dangerous waterway no longer reporting incidents directly. UK Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) admitted in its...
articles.body: Containers Dry Cargo Gas Middle East Operations Tankers Hormuz attacks overwhelm UKMTO Sam Chambers October 19, 2026 0 854 2 minutes read Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps The sheer volume of attacks on commercial shipping around the Strait of Hormuz has left Britain’s maritime security reporting centre struggling to keep track, with most vessels targeted in the increasingly dangerous waterway no longer reporting incidents directly. UK Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) admitted in its latest weekly assessment that it is “struggling to accurately report true number of attacks”, warning that the majority of vessels attacked are refusing to report incidents. The organisation said it was aware of further attacks through other sources but could not include them in its figures without verification UKMTO has recorded 135 incidents related to the Iran-US conflict since hostilities began on February 28, including 114 reports of vessel damage and 76 people killed or injured. Twelve attacks were recorded in its latest weekly assessment, ten in Hormuz itself, one in the Arabian Gulf and another in the Gulf of Oman. Of the vessels involved, one was lost, two were disabled and three had unconfirmed outcomes. The violence has continued through the weekend, with attacks spreading well beyond the narrow confines of Hormuz. On Friday, the 302,977 dwt VLCC ST3 was struck by an unidentified projectile approximately 68 nautical miles northeast of Al Jubail, Saudi Arabia. The Marshall Islands-flagged tanker suffered an engine room fire and lost power, according to maritime security firm Vanguard. All 15 Indian seafarers aboard were safely evacuated to a nearby UAE-flagged containership. Later on Friday, another tanker was attacked approximately 78 nautical miles northeast of Al Jubail, this time by a rocket-propelled grenade fired from a small boat. The projectile damaged the vessel’s aft port quarter. All crewmembers were reported safe, although the full extent of the damage remains unclear. Saturday brought further alarming claims from Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC), which said two fully laden supertankers, each carrying more than 2m barrels of crude, had struck naval mines while attempting to transit Hormuz without Iranian authorisation. The IRGC claimed both vessels caught fire, with one suffering a major engine room explosion that left it immobilised. Neither ship has been identified and no independent confirmation has emerged. In its latest assessment, the Joint Maritime Information Center (JMIC) explicitly stated that there was no substantiation for the Iranian claims. On Sunday, a tug travelling south approximately 20 nautical miles northeast of Khorfakkan was struck by two unidentified projectiles. One crewmember sustained minor injuries and the tug suffered damage, although it was able to continue its voyage. A further security incident was reported on Saturday in the Gulf of Aden, where an LNG carrier was approached by a skiff carrying seven people. Two shots were fired at the gas carrier before its armed security team returned warning shots, forcing the attackers to withdraw. Maritime authorities are treating that incident as suspected piracy rather than a confirmed Iranian attack. Despite the extraordinary violence, oil continues to move. Signal Ocean data shows approximately 13.9m barrels per day of crude and another 2.3m barrels per day of oil products still passing through Hormuz. Scandinavian bank SEB argued in a new report today that the disruption is “more a risk-premium story than a volume blockage”, with oil continuing to move through the shuttle system established to maintain exports. The distinction between cargo volumes and vessel movements is significant. UKMTO’s latest figures show 254 vessel transits in a week, approximately 70% below pre-war levels. JMIC reported around 217 vessels waiting at anchor near Fujairah and Khorfakkan on Sunday, with congestion continuing to build outside the strait. articles.body: Maersk has completed what it describes as the world’s largest ethanol bunkering operation, supplying approximately 5,000 metric tonnes of ISCC-certified bioethanol to Maersk Halifax in Singapore. The operation marks the first ethanol bunkering of a retrofitted vessel in Maersk’s fleet. Maersk Halifax is the company’s first container ship to be converted to dual-fuel operation. The bunkering was carried out in collaboration with the Maritime and Port Authority of Singapore (MPA) and other industry partners. According to Maersk, the project provided operational experience involving ethanol infrastructure, sourcing, supply-chain readiness and vessel operations. Maersk advances multi-fuel strategy Maersk views ethanol as one of several potential fuel pathways for reducing emissions from ocean transportation. The carrier said ethanol benefits from established production and distribution networks, global availability and compatibility with alcohol-enabled engine technologies. When produced through certified low-carbon pathways, the fuel can offer greenhouse gas reductions compared with conventional marine fuels. “The energy transition requires us to explore and scale solutions that can deliver real-world impact. At Maersk, we continue to pursue a multi-fuel strategy because we recognise that no single fuel pathway can decarbonise global shipping on its own,” said Emma Mazhari, Head of Energy Markets at Maersk. The Singapore operation follows earlier ethanol trials involving Laura Maersk, Antonia Maersk and Tangier Maersk. Maersk recently completed the first ship-to-ship commercial ethanol bunkering of a deep-sea container vessel in the United States, using US-produced corn ethanol aboard Tangier Maersk. The latest operation expands the carrier’s practical experience with ethanol while assessing the infrastructure and supply-chain requirements needed for its wider use as a marine fuel.

articles.title: Nordic energy players hit paydirt with new gas and condensate discovery
articles.summary: Vår Energi and Equinor have struck gas and condensate in Norwegian waters, packing up to 5.5 million barrels.
articles.body: Exploration & Production October 19, 2026 · 4 hours ago Nordic energy players hit paydirt with new gas and condensate discovery Vår Energi and Equinor have struck gas and condensate in Norwegian waters, packing up to 5.5 million barrels. MC Melisa Cavcic Senior Editor 2 minutes read LinkedIn X Email COSL Prospector rig Source: COSL Norway’s energy duo, Vår Energi and Equinor, have made a gas and condensate find in a new Norwegian Sea license, uncovering a fresh prospect estimated to hold up to 5.5 million barrels of oil equivalent (boe). Vår Energi and Equinor have made a gas and condensate discovery in the 6407/5-3 S well, which is known as the Lakris prospect in the Gimsan Basin on the Halten Terrace in the Norwegian Sea. This wildcat well was drilled about 170 kilometers northwest of Kristiansund as the first exploration well in production license 1002 , which was awarded in the APA 2018 round on March 1, 2019. The licensees in the production license are Vår Energi (operator) and Equinor, which drilled the well 6407/5-3 S using the COSL Prospector semi-submersible rig to a vertical depth of 4,225 meters below sea level and terminated in the Lower Jurassic. The water depth at the site is 218 meters. The well, which was not formation-tested, but data and samples were collected, will now be permanently plugged and abandoned. The objective of the well was to prove petroleum in chalk reservoir rocks in the Nise Formation, as well as in Lower Jurassic reservoir rocks in the Tilje Formation. Based on the Norwegian Offshore Directorate’s data, hydrocarbon shows were proven in the lower Tilje Formation. The well did not encounter a sandstone reservoir in the Nise Formation, but elevated gas values were recorded in the interval. The Garn, Ile, and Tofte formations were also investigated, but the intervals were aquiferous, and the reservoir quality was moderate to poor. The well 6407/5-3 S encountered gas and condensate in the upper Tilje Formation in heterolithic reservoir rocks, totalling 54 meters, with moderate to poor reservoir quality. The gas/water contact was not encountered in the well. The preliminary calculations indicate the size of the discovery is between 0.2 and 0.9 million standard cubic meters of recoverable oil equivalent, which corresponds to between 1.3 and 5.5 million barrels of oil equivalent. The latest hydrocarbon find in Norwegian waters comes months after Equinor, Aker BP, and Vår Energi teamed up to look for major hydrocarbon discoveries on the Norwegian Continental Shelf (NCS). Focus on growth and infrastructure As CEO, Huck will focus on increasing cargo volumes, improving port operations and supporting further investment in infrastructure and technology. articles.title: Readers Speak: Joint ventures lead preferences for container terminal operations
articles.summary: The role of foreign companies in operating major container terminals remains a subject of debate, particularly when international investment intersects with national interests and the management of strategic infrastructure. In its latest Readers Speak poll, Container News asked readers whether foreign companies...
articles.body: The role of foreign companies in operating major container terminals remains a subject of debate, particularly when international investment intersects with national interests and the management of strategic infrastructure. In its latest Readers Speak poll, Container News asked readers whether foreign companies should operate major container terminals. The results revealed a preference for joint ventures, suggesting that many readers favour arrangements combining international participation with domestic involvement. Other approaches, including unrestricted foreign operations and operations subject to safeguards, also attracted support, while exclusively domestic operations represented a smaller share of the overall response. Joint ventures emerge as the preferred approach Joint ventures emerged as the leading choice, highlighting an apparent preference for cooperation between international operators and domestic partners. This result may reflect the importance readers place on maintaining local involvement in terminal operations while allowing international companies to contribute operational expertise and investment. Rather than favouring either unrestricted foreign participation or complete domestic control, the strongest response points towards a model in which responsibilities and interests are shared. However, the preference for joint ventures should not be interpreted as a consensus that they are the only acceptable operating structure. The results reveal a range of views on how foreign participation should be organised. Safeguards remain an important consideration Allowing foreign companies to operate container terminals under safeguards also attracted meaningful support. This suggests that some readers are comfortable with international operators taking a more direct role, provided appropriate conditions and oversight are maintained. The distinction between this approach and joint ventures is significant. While joint ventures involve a particular partnership structure, safeguards could apply to different operating arrangements. Together, these responses suggest considerable interest in foreign participation accompanied by mechanisms intended to protect domestic interests. Unrestricted operations and domestic control attract differing views A substantial group of readers supported allowing foreign companies to operate major container terminals freely. This position may reflect confidence in international terminal operators and a preference for fewer restrictions on commercial participation. At the other end of the discussion, some readers favoured limiting operations exclusively to domestic companies. That response suggests continued concern about the role of foreign businesses in infrastructure considered strategically important. Nevertheless, the broader results indicate that neither unrestricted foreign operations nor complete exclusion of foreign operators emerged as the dominant position. How this fits into the broader Readers Speak trend The latest Readers Speak findings extend the discussion of shipping resilience, port infrastructure and global connectivity into the question of who should operate critical maritime facilities. Previous polls have highlighted the importance readers place on strong shipping networks and effective port infrastructure. This week’s results introduce an additional consideration: the structure through which international companies participate in terminal operations. The preference for joint ventures suggests that many readers see cooperation between domestic and foreign interests as an attractive approach. At the same time, support for safeguards and unrestricted operations demonstrates that views on foreign involvement are not uniform. Ultimately, the results suggest that the debate is less about whether international operators should participate in container terminal operations and more about the conditions and structures under which that participation should take place.

articles.body: CEVA Logistics has announced the integration of Colis Privé and PAACK under a single brand, strengthening its last-mile delivery services across Europe. The combined business will operate under the PAACK name and serve five countries: France, Belgium, Luxembourg, Spain and Portugal. Together, the two networks handle approximately 150 million parcels each year and operate more than 17,000 out-of-home delivery points. The move aims to simplify cross-border deliveries for e-commerce retailers and improve coordination between the two networks. Expanding European delivery services The integration brings together Colis Privé’s established delivery network and PAACK’s technology capabilities. The combined network includes around 8,000 delivery points in France, 1,500 in Belgium and 8,000 in Spain. CEVA Logistics expects the unified operation to help retailers manage deliveries across several European markets through a single network. The companies have already introduced their first joint delivery solution for a major international retailer. According to CEVA, this service combines the capabilities of both businesses to support deliveries across multiple countries. The PAACK brand will be introduced gradually to customers and partners from January 2027. Supporting CMA CGM’s logistics strategy The integration also supports the wider logistics strategy of CEVA Logistics and its parent company, CMA CGM Group. By combining the two delivery networks, CEVA aims to strengthen its services across the supply chain, from international freight transport and warehousing to final delivery. The move will also allow the company to offer e-commerce customers a broader range of delivery options across Europe. CEVA said the unified business will focus on reliable delivery services, technology and closer coordination between its European operations.

Paula Olson/NOAA Fisheries/Handout via REUTERS By Ana Isabel Martinez and Sarah Morland MEXICO CITY, Oct 18 (Reuters) – Mexico’s president said on Thursday a drastic reduction in the protected area for the near-extinct vaquita marina, the world’s smallest porpoise, will help fishing communities. Critics say this week’s reduction in the area where fishermen cannot use gillnets, long walls of nylon mesh, by 86% to 1,562 square kilometers (603 square miles), about the size of Greater London, threatens the survival of the species. The prior agreement had protected an area similar to the size of the US state of Connecticut. President Claudia Sheinbaum said the new scope aimed to protect biodiversity in the Gulf of California while also allowing fishermen to make a better living. Authorities said the measure took into account proposals by the International Committee for the Recovery of the Vaquita, a government advisory body. Lorenzo Rojas-Bracho, a Mexican marine biologist and leading vaquita expert who took part in the committee, said he hoped a smaller area could concentrate efforts to save the mammal. “It is difficult to enforce a ban over a very large area, which includes vast areas with no recent records of vaquitas,” Rojas-Bracho told Reuters. “If you lose a ring you don’t search your entire house, you focus on where you lost it.” Scientists estimated last year there were just 7 to 10 vaquitas left, including at least one calf. The population has collapsed from around 600 in 1997, largely due to illegal fishing targeting totoaba, whose swim bladders are highly prized in Chinese medicine and can fetch up to $10,000 in Asia. Rojas-Bracho said that if no more vaquitas are killed, the remaining handful of porpoises would have a good chance of repopulating the species. However, he said the area needs more effective tracking of fishing boats, better monitoring and that fishermen should use alternative methods that do not put the vaquita at risk. Gerardo Ceballos, a biologist at the National Autonomous University of Mexico, said allowing the vaquita to become extinct would amount to a moral failure. “What’s happening to the vaquita is a death foretold,” he said. “We’ve reduced the vaquita’s protected area without actually having the technical or logistical capacity to enforce regulations there; we’re giving in to pressure from interested groups so a larger area can be exploited.” Ceballos said a very minimal government investment would ensure the vaquita’s protection. As things currently stood, however, he believed theporpoise was on the path to extinction. “If the vaquita goes extinct it won’t solve insecurity or poverty or any of the local problems. And Mexico would lose an icon,” he said. “If actions are taken, there is a possibility, a hope. And we must keep working with hope.” (Reporting by Ana Isabel Martinez and Sarah Morland in Mexico City; Editing by Stephen Coates and Alexander Smith) (c) Copyright Thomson Reuters 202 6. articles.body: The Port of Rotterdam recorded a 0.9% increase in total cargo throughput during the first nine months of 2026, reaching 323.2 million tonnes. Container throughput remained largely stable, rising by 0.1% in TEU compared with the same period last year. However, container volumes measured in tonnes declined by 2.2%. The figures also showed a sharp decline in transshipment activity, while container traffic to and from the European hinterland continued to grow. Transshipment falls as hinterland traffic increases Container transshipment at Rotterdam fell by 20% during the nine-month period. According to the Port of Rotterdam Authority, capacity constraints at deep-sea terminals have led to more cargo being handled through other ports. This has created additional space for containers moving to and from the hinterland. Hinterland container volumes increased by 7.2%, supported by an 8.9% rise in full container imports. Full container exports also grew, although at a slower rate of 1%. As imports increased faster than exports, the movement of empty containers continued to rise. Bulk cargo supports overall growth Dry bulk throughput increased by 2.1%, supported by higher coal volumes and demand for construction materials. Coal throughput rose by 15.3%, while iron ore and scrap declined by 5.9%. Liquid bulk volumes grew by 3.1%. Crude oil throughput increased by 2.1%, while mineral oil products recorded growth of 11.1%. LNG throughput edged down by 0.2%, while breakbulk volumes fell by 1.4%. Boudewijn Siemons, CEO of the Port of Rotterdam Authority, highlighted the importance of reliable transport connections as European trade flows continue to change. “Reliable infrastructure is the basis for economic growth and a resilient supply chain,” said Siemons. The port authority stressed the need for continued investment in road, rail and inland waterway connections to support European trade and improve supply chain resilience.

Swedish Coast Guard/Handout via TT News Agency/via REUTERS By Karin Matussek Oct 18, 2026 (Bloomberg) –A Ukrainian army officer suspected of being a protagonist in the sabotage of Nord Stream gas pipelines in 2022 stood trial in Hamburg accused of committing a war crime. The man, identified as 50-year-old Serhii K., was chosen by Ukraine authorities to lead the operation, prosecutor Stefan Schmidt said on the first day of trial. Serhii K. was arrested in Italy a year ago and extradited to Germany. “He had the mandate and authorization from the Ukraine government,” prosecutor Schmidt said. The crucial pipelines ferried gas from Russia through the Baltic Sea to Lubmin, a costal city in the North East of Germany. Serhii K. was an officer in the Ukrainian Army. After Russia invaded the country in February 2022, he and other military personnel, acting on behalf of Ukrainian government agencies, devised a plan to destroy the Nord Stream 1 and 2 natural gas pipelines , according to the indictment. The goal was to permanently halt gas deliveries via the pipelines and prevent Russia from using the revenue from gas trades to finance its war efforts. To carry out the plan, Serhii K. allegedly lead a group of professional divers, a boat captain skipper and an explosives expert. In early September 2022, the crew entered a sailing yacht which had been rented in Rostock, Germany, using forged identification documents. With the ship, the men transported explosives for military use to a location near the Danish island of Bornholm. In the weeks leading up to the attack Serhii K.’s group attached various explosive devices with time fuses to the pipelines. They detonated on September 26, 2022. Serhii K.’s lawyers rejected the allegations. Nicola Canestrini, a defense lawyer for Serhii K., said Germany can’t try his client for a war crime because that wasn’t covered by the Italian extradition ruling granted only for a sabotage charges. No one was hurt or killed by the incident and Germany tragically mistakes who the real perpetrators are, Canestrini told the court. “After Bucha, Mariupol, and the abducted Ukrainian children, he’s the first person the German authorities are trying as a war criminal—not a Russian, but an officer in the armed forces defending against a war of aggression,” he said. Russia had used the pipeline as a military, financial and political weapon in the war , so defining it as a merely civilian object was wrong, he added. There was also no direct evidence, like finger prints or DNA, that proved Serhii K. was on the yacht, Canestrini said. The indirect evidence prosecutors are now citing was illegally transferred from Italy to Germany without proper judicial authorization. Serhii K.’s lawyers asked the court to drop the case because his Ukrainian military superiors didn’t allow him speak about details of his service and disclosing them would be a crime under Ukrainian law. Since he can’t properly defend himself now, the trial must be discontinued, they argued. Speculation had swirled about the origin of the attacks on the pipelines, installed to deliver natural gas from Russia to Germany under the Baltic Sea. The incident triggered a wave of accusations, with Russia blaming it on sabotage by the US, Ukraine and Poland, calling them “beneficiaries” of the blasts. The Nord Stream 1 undersea link to Germany was the main route for Russian pipeline gas flows before the Kremlin’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine, while the second pipeline was completed but never went operational. In 2021, the year before the war started, Nord Stream 1 delivered more than a third of Russia’s total gas exports to Europe. A central point of disagreement has been Washington’s insistence on addressing Iran’s nuclear program from the outset. US Vice President JD Vance said earlier this month that Iran must make a “meaningful” reduction in its uranium enrichment capacity to satisfy US demands and end the countries’ eight-month war. Tehran says negotiations should initially focus on reopening the Strait of Hormuz , which before the war carried about a fifth of the global trade in oil and liquefied natural gas (LNG), and restoring security in the waterway. articles.title: Fincantieri Integrates AI, Robotics to Advance Shipyards
articles.summary: Fincantieri is accelerating the transformation of its shipyards through the integration of advanced robotics, Physical AI, and next-generation automation systems, with the aim of making production processes increasingly efficient, safe, and…
articles.body: Fincantieri Integrates AI, Robotics to Advance Shipyards Maritime Activity Reports, Inc. October 16, 2026 Credit: Fincantieri Fincantieri is accelerating the transformation of its shipyards through the integration of advanced robotics, Physical AI, and next-generation automation systems, with the aim of making production processes increasingly efficient, safe, and competitive. This is the vision behind BOOST² – The Shipyard of the Future, the industrial innovation program launched by the Group three years ago to identify, develop, and integrate new technologies into its production processes. Throughout its journey, the initiative has engaged more than 450 Fincantieri employees across 13 shipyards in Italy and abroad, including facilities in Romania and the United States, fostering direct interaction with operational needs and actively involving people in the development of new solutions. As part of the Industrial Plan, the program provides for investments of almost 100 million euros. The program’s latest achievements were presented at the Castellammare di Stabia shipyard through demonstrations of solutions already in operation, technologies currently undergoing validation, and applications destined for further evolution. Following an initial phase focused on technology scouting and experimentation, the program is now geared towards accelerating the transition from innovation to industrial deployment, supporting the adoption of new solutions in day-to-day operations and their progressive rollout across the Group’s shipyards. This approach builds on the results achieved so far and aims to further strengthen the integration of technologies, industrial expertise, and the practical needs of production. In this context, collaboration with the innovation ecosystem plays a key role. Through its Open Innovation strategy, Fincantieri identifies and selects technology partners in Italy and internationally, including SMEs and start-ups, to develop and tailor solutions to the specific needs of the shipbuilding industry. The direct involvement of people and production teams is an integral part of the process, enabling field testing, accelerating adoption, and ensuring that technologies can be scaled and replicated across different manufacturing environments. At the heart of the program are Physical AI, which enables intelligent systems to interact with the physical world, and collaborative robotics, with applications designed to support people in carrying out the most complex tasks. These technologies are complemented by Digital Twin solutions for the digital management of shipyard assets and processes, Smart Supply Chain systems, additive manufacturing, and automated solutions for industrial equipment. The objective is to unlock the full potential of these technologies by progressively integrating them into operational workflows and strengthening the connection between design, planning, and production.

articles.body: Oil Prices Rise by More Than 3% Maritime Activity Reports, Inc. October 16, 2026 Credit: Adobe Stock/hunterpic2013 Oil prices gained more than 3% and were heading for weekly gains on continued uncertainty over Middle East supplies, and as investors kept assessing how much diesel Russia could supply to the global markets. Brent crude futures were up $3.41, or 3.2%, at $109.34 at 12:41 p.m. ET (1641 GMT), while US West Texas Intermediate crude futures rose $2.74, or 2.8%, to $100.67, crossing $100 for the first time since September 21. So far this week, Brent has risen 4.1% and WTI 8.6%. "Conflict in the Middle East still keeps coming back and I think it's questionable how much diesel fuel Russia can actually deliver to the markets. Those two factors are just continuing to have traders be buyers," said Dennis Kissler, senior vice president of trading at BOK Financial. Supply concerns also increased as attacks around the Strait of Hormuz surged over the past 10 days, with Iran saying it was stepping up strikes in response to the US blockade of its ports and tougher sanctions introduced last month. Yemen's Houthis also fired missiles at the presidential palace complex in the southern city of Aden on Thursday, killing five people. "Intensified Iranian attacks drove Gulf crude flows sharply lower," Kpler analysts said in a report on Thursday, adding that they expected a slower and more uneven recovery in Hormuz flows in the absence of a comprehensive political deal. Meanwhile, Ukraine struck a Russian oil refinery on Thursday after President Volodymyr Zelenskiy declared that Kyiv was abandoning a ceasefire covering energy sites announced by US President Donald Trump and criticised Trump's willingness to strike deals with Moscow. Russia's Ryazan oil refinery has suspended operations at a primary crude distillation unit following a drone attack in the region on Thursday, two industry sources told Reuters. The IEA agreed on Thursday to release more than 20 million barrels of fuel to the market. Those margins rose as high as $95 a barrel in September as diesel supply tightened because of the wars in Ukraine and Iran. Brent crude was little changed on Thursday, while WTI settled up more than 3% after news that the US was weighing plans to ease restrictions on the world’s "shadow fleet" of tankers and after a big US crude stock draw on hurricane production shut-ins. articles.title: All American Marine Build Report: October 2026
articles.summary: All American Marine recently launched M/V North Star, the second high-speed, long-range eco-tour vessel built for Phillips Cruises & Tours. Like her sistership, Chugach Express, North Star will operate from Whittier, Alaska, carrying passengers…
articles.body: All American Marine Build Report: October 2026 Maritime Activity Reports, Inc. Ron Wille, President, All American Marine October 16, 2026 Credit: AAM All American Marine recently launched M/V North Star, the second high-speed, long-range eco-tour vessel built for Phillips Cruises & Tours. Like her sistership, Chugach Express, North Star will operate from Whittier, Alaska, carrying passengers through the tidewater glaciers and wildlife-filled waters of Prince William Sound. The 84.5-foot, hydrofoil-assisted aluminum catamaran features a Teknicraft Design semi-displacement hull and is certified to USCG Subchapter T standards for up to 150 passengers. Her propulsion package mirrors that of Chugach Express: four MJP 350X waterjets driven by quad 800 mhp Scania DI16 082M engines, paired with Teknicraft’s dynamic hydrofoil system and wave-piercing bow. A repeat order is performance data in its clearest form. After operating Chugach Express through three demanding Alaska seasons, with full passenger loads, long days, and changing conditions. Phillips knew this platform could deliver. One of the most notable changes is fuel capacity with Chugach Express carrying 1,200 gallons, while North Star carries 1,600. The increase did not require a redesign; it was made possible by proven performance. Chugach Express demonstrated that the hull could carry additional weight without sacrificing speed, efficiency, or ride quality. The second vessel uses that margin to add 400 gallons and extend its operating range. But range is only part of the story. The Teknicraft hull and dynamic hydrofoil system are designed to reduce vessel accelerations underway, while the hull form and foil provide added motion damping at rest. For passengers, that means a more comfortable ride. For operators, it means a broader usable weather window, supporting more operating days, greater schedule reliability, and stronger revenue potential. That capability matters in Prince William Sound. Maintaining comfortable speeds in changing sea conditions can preserve more time at the destination while keeping the return schedule within reach. It can also mean the difference between completing a tour and remaining at the dock. Last month, we examined how little fuel consumption changes between light and fully loaded conditions on a Teknicraft hull. North Star shows what an operator can do with that margin. Greater fuel capacity, strong seakeeping, and efficient performance combine to create something more valuable than any single specification: greater operating capacity. WHAT OPERATORS ARE ASKING Top speed tells only part of the story. Passenger vessel operators need to know how a vessel rides at full load in real conditions, how guests feel after five or six hours aboard, and how much of the schedule can be maintained when the weather turns. Those are seakeeping questions, and on a tour vessel, they show up in two places. The first is underway. During transit, the Teknicraft hull form and hydrofoil lift work together to reduce vertical accelerations, the pounding and slamming that wear on passengers and crew over a long day. The second is on scene. At a glacier’s face or alongside a pod of humpbacks, low-speed motion is often when passengers begin to feel unwell. Here, the hull form and foil help dampen that motion. Guests stay on deck, crews remain ready to work, and fewer people become what one of our operators calls “mal de mer zombies.” One additional advantage comes in the adjustable hydrofoil. By de-tuning it, captains can make the vessel ride “heavier” at wildlife-viewing speeds, settling the hull and creating a steadier viewing platform. The vessel remains light and fuel-efficient during transit, then becomes more planted once on scene. Weather is where seakeeping becomes operating capacity. These hulls can maintain comfortable speeds in conditions that force other vessels to slow down or remain at the dock. That broader operating window supports more completed trips, greater schedule reliability, and stronger revenue potential. WHAT IT SIGNALS As Alaska’s tour season winds down, passenger vessel operators head into the off-season with a full season of results in hand. That is when a vessel should be evaluated, by what it delivered through months of real service. What these operators have learned is straightforward: comfort is operating capacity. A vessel that can sail comfortably in more conditions completes more departures, issues fewer refunds, and protects revenue. A vessel that remains steady at low speed keeps guests on deck and engaged. A hull with additional carrying capacity gives operators options, and Phillips Cruises and Tours chose to turn that margin into greater range. Real performance is measured across the entire operating day: at full load, through a full season, and in the weather operators encounter, not the weather they started the season wishing for.

articles.body: Incat Crowther to Build Fourth Fast Support Intervention Vessel Maritime Activity Reports, Inc. October 16, 2026 Credit: Incat Crowther Zamil Offshore commissioned Incat Crowther and Singaporean shipbuilder Lita Ocean to design, build and deliver a fourth 60-m ABS-classed monohull Fast Support Intervention Vessel (FSIV). The project follows the delivery of the third vessel in the original fleet with the performance of the fleet leading to the order of a fourth vessel. The FSIV fleet is assisting Zamil Offshore with the efficient and safe transport of cargo, heavy maintenance equipment and personnel for Saudi Aramco’s operations in the Arabian Sea. Capable of speeds up to 36 knots, the vessels are powered by four MTU 16V4000 diesel engines coupled to ZF gearboxes driving Hamilton HT810 waterjets . Maneuverability of the DP2-certified vessels is enhanced by three Hydromaster tunnel bow thrusters , allowing safe docking and offshore station-keeping for transfer of cargo and personnel. Two of the main engines are coupled to FFS firefighting pumps paired with 1200 cu. m./hr. water monitors and shipboard water spray protection offering FiFi-1 capability. Three Scania 300kW diesel generators provide ship service power. The main deck offers an expansive 250 sq. m. aft cargo deck rated at 2.5 t/ m2 along with an optional Palfinger PK12000M deck crane . A climate-controlled forward cabin features business-class seating for 56 service personnel, as well as two bathrooms, a 15 sq. m. workshop, a 15 sq. m. storage room, a lounge and snack bar. The crew of 20 on the vessel are housed on the hull deck which features a large pantry, mess, three bathrooms and two laundry rooms. The vessels comply with the latest MCVSR requirements from Saudi Aramco, including ABS SMART notation . Construction is now underway on the fourth vessel, with the vessel set to join its predecessors in service by 2027.

articles.title: Singapore Conducts Oil Spill Response Drill
articles.summary: Singapore, Indonesia and Malaysia conducted a ground deployment exercise (GDX) under the Revolving Fund Committee to strengthen coordination in responding to oil spills in the Straits of Malacca and Singapore. Conducted ahead of Singapore’s 17th Joint Oil Spill Exercise (JOSE) 2026…
articles.body: Singapore Conducts Oil Spill Response Drill Maritime Activity Reports, Inc. October 16, 2026 Credit: Adobe Stock/Peter Hermes Furian Singapore, Indonesia and Malaysia conducted a ground deployment exercise (GDX) under the Revolving Fund Committee to strengthen coordination in responding to oil spills in the Straits of Malacca and Singapore. Conducted ahead of Singapore’s 17th Joint Oil Spill Exercise (JOSE) 2026, the GDX simulated an oil spill originating from a vessel collision in Singapore waters, with the oil subsequently reaching the shores of Indonesia and Malaysia. Led by the Maritime and Port Authority of Singapore (MPA), the GDX tested information sharing, response planning and mutual assistance among the three littoral States. As part of the exercise, Indonesia and Malaysia deployed response assets in their respective waters to test their response arrangements under the exercise scenario. Separately, MPA hosted representatives from government agencies, industry partners and international organisations at the Integrated Operations Hub (IOH) Lab at ALICE@Mediapolis as part of JOSE 2026. The program provided an opportunity to share Singapore’s oil spill response capabilities and explore how emerging technologies could support future response operations. Representatives from the International Maritime Organization (IMO), ITOPF[1], Indonesia’s Directorate General of Sea Transportation and Malaysia’s Department of Environment also attended the program. Participants were briefed on the coordinated deployment of response assets for oil containment, dispersal and recovery, drawing on demonstrations conducted at sea. The program also highlighted how emerging technologies could enhance oil spill response. These included MPA’s Maritime Digital Twin (MDT), which uses modelling to predict the movement of spilled oil and identify potentially affected areas, as well as artificial intelligence to support response planning and resource deployment. Participants were also briefed on potential concepts of operations involving unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) and unmanned surface vessels (USVs), including those trialled with ST Engineering. Drawing on demonstrations conducted at sea, the briefing illustrated how aerial surveillance could guide USVs in carrying out tasks such as dispersant spraying and oil containment boom towing. Overall, JOSE explored how such concepts of operations could be supported as unmanned technologies mature, potentially expanding the range of capabilities available for future oil spill response operations.
